newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas-92-octane mogas traded at $22.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas-92-octane mogas traded at $22.

text.p: Gasoline prices on Wednesday moved lower amid talks that levels may have hit a floor and are on their way up in the near term, traders said.
A 50,000-barrel of 92-octane supplies were sold by a European major to a western trader at $22.00 a barrel for July 10-14 loading.
The same European major was offering 50,000 barrels of 92-octane supplies at $22.50 for July 8-12 loading on Tuesday.
Traders said the trade, which was done at 50 cents below the previous day quotes were indicative that the market is still weak.
But the buyer said prices are likely to move higher in July with Indonesia expected to soak up some supplies as two of their refineries undergo maintenance shutdown.
He said he would sell the same cargo later at higher prices.

Another parcel of similar grade supplies was heard traded at a 50 cent discount to Singapore spot quotes fob Singapore by a Singapore refiner. "Bids went in at a discount of between $0.50-$1.00," said one trader.
The naphtha market was quiet. The start-up delay of a condensate splitter in Indonesia is expected to spark naphtha demand from Indonesia.
Mobil receives heavy naphtha produced from the splitter.
Taiwan is expected to award its tender to buy 28,000 tonnes of August napthenic and aromatic naphtha for August 1-31 delivery on Thursday.
